messages:
maya: Heads-up — customer ACME (ticket #7892) reports a sharp output-quality regression after today's rollout at ~09:00 UTC. Previously concise policy answers now include fabricated citations and incorrect process steps. Example below. :rotating_light:

ashley: I have the before/after outputs and the customer's repro prompt. Pasted snippets below. Customer says this started immediately after your rollout. https://support.redwood.com/ticket/7892 :eyes:

deploy-bot: rollout job r-20260322-19 for model rwd-legal-2023 status: SUCCESS @ 2026-03-22T09:01:07Z

olga: Which exact model/version was rolled? commit hash or build tag? @devon you merged the inference change earlier, right?

devon: yep — merged PR #4127. Summary: switch to new kernel selection + small kv-cache refactor + a quantized execution path toggle (opt-in runtime flag). No intentional temp/top-k changes.

liam: Can we repro? Need the prompt, model config (max_tokens, temperature, top_p) and any runtime flags. Also please grab a trace (request id) if available.

ashley: Repro prompt (sanitized):
```
Prompt: "What are the legal steps for terminating a vendor contract due to non-performance? Provide citations and timelines."

BEFORE (v2.3.1):
- Clear checklist with 5 steps, references to statute X, recommended timelines 30–60 days, no fabricated case names.

AFTER (v2.4.0 rolled 09:00):
- Long answer with specific-sounding case citations (made-up), inaccurate timelines, and a confident-sounding but wrong step about filing "Notice Z" which doesn't exist.
```
Request ID: req_20260322_acme_21

maya: Customer included examples and said they paused integration traffic after seeing 3 clients reject responses. They're asking for rollback and root cause.

olga: That output pattern looks like context misalignment (model reading prompt incorrectly) or a decoding/penalty change. The PR touched kv-cache indexing for offset handling — if older cached prefixes are misaligned it could splice in unrelated tokens.

devon: Confirmed PR diff: change in kv offset math + runtime flag to enable int8 path. If kv offsets are off by a token it could produce hallucinated context.

olga: Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert to v2.3.1 pinned model image for production; 2) disable quantized execution flag cluster-wide; 3) hotpatch fix to kv offset math. Revert is fastest.

liam: Rolling a rollback must pass through capacity checks. I can trigger a canary revert on one host first and validate with ACME's prompt. If green, full rollback.

devon: Agree. Do canary revert -> run customer prompt -> compare against v2.3.1 baseline. If mismatch persists, we escalate to hotpatch.

olga: I already built a v2.3.1 artifact available as tag v2.3.1-rc1 on the private registry. Command to rollback (ops):
```bash
# rollback model to previous pinned version
redwood deploy rollback --model-id rwd-legal-2023 --to-version v2.3.1 --scope canary --reason "regression/ACME ticket 7892"
```

liam: Kicking off canary rollback now.

deploy-bot: rollback job r-rollback-20260322-21 submitted by liam @ 2026-03-22T09:12:14Z

deploy-bot: canary rollback node-7 -> v2.3.1 started

liam: Canary node finished deploy. Running the ACME prompt against canary...

liam: Canary output matches BEFORE baseline (v2.3.1). No fabricated citations. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary rollback r-rollback-20260322-21 status: SUCCESS on node-7 @ 2026-03-22T09:22:03Z

liam: Proceeding with cluster-wide rollback now.

deploy-bot: rollback job r-rollback-20260322-21 progressing: 3/12 nodes completed

deploy-bot: rollback job r-rollback-20260322-21 completed: ALL NODES -> v2.3.1 @ 2026-03-22T09:45:20Z

olga: Opening hotfix branch with unit/regression tests to cover kv-cache offset edge cases. PR #4132 created (will include additional asserts and a migration check).

devon: I'll cherry-pick the safe tests into a CI job and run full integration.

maya: Notified ACME: apologized, rolled back, offered 5 days of credits and a dedicated follow-up. Ticket updated with timeline and rollback job ids.

ashley: Customer responded: "Thanks, we see correct behavior again. Please let us know root cause and ETA for permanent fix."

olga: ETA for patch review + QA ~48 hours. Will prioritize.

liam: I'll keep monitoring related request ids and surface any anomalies in the next 24h.

maya: Closing loop with support doc updates: add a short KB entry on rollback steps and mitigation playbook.

devon: Follow-up action items: 1) PR #4132 review, 2) run quantized-path fuzz against vendor prompts, 3) postmortem with timeline. Tagging ops/security for audit of rollout approvals. :shipit:

maya: Thanks team — great triage. :white_check_mark:
